CT is not a reliable method for determining the level of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) block in tuberculous hydrocephalus. While it can provide images of the brain and spinal cord, it does not have the ability to accurately measure or diagnose CSF block.

The retrieved matches indicate that CT scans are not useful for assessing the extent of CSF obstruction in tuberculous hydrocephalus. Instead, air-encephalography remains the most reliable method for determining the level of CSF obstruction.

This is because CT scans provide a two-dimensional view of the brain and spinal cord, whereas CSF block creates a three-dimensional space that cannot be accurately visualized by a CT scan. Furthermore, CT scans do not allow for the measurement or assessment of the degree of CSF block, which is essential for diagnosing tuberculous hydrocephalus.

Therefore, it is recommended to use air-encephalography as the primary method for assessing the level of CSF block in tuberculous hydrocephalus.
